translation_notes: IDENTITY translation: translated.ldpy is byte-for-byte original.py. The region builds no RDF term at all — it parses an expected graph from a file, materialises a mapping with morph-kgc and compares by isomorphism — so no island applies. Every valid Python program being a valid ldpy program, the pair is trivially equivalent; the interesting datum is the negative one: an example classified 'high' on RDF-op density (graph_ctor + serialize_parse) where the notation has nothing to offer.

data files: mapping.ttl and output.nq (a few lines each, Apache-2.0) copied from test/rml-in-memory/json_dictionary/RMLIMTC0000/ next to the example, because the region resolves them from os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)) and both representations sit in the same directory; no other change
the test is degenerate by design (the input dictionary has an empty 'students' list, so morph-kgc generates 0 triples and output.nq is empty) — it runs morph-kgc for real on both sides
driver: single fixture, the test takes no argument; equivalence is the identical assertion outcome
